messages.author: 51708af3af54863b
messages.subject: Shiny Dashboard and HTML
parts:
I have a general question about how HTML works with Shiny Dashboard. Styling with a custom CSS referencing an external file is very straightforward, but I'm having trouble understanding how adding custom HTML referencing an external HTML file works. For example, for CSS I just use the described code: tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css", href = "custom.css"), which is very easy and straighforward. But, I'm having difficult doing the same thing with HTML. For example, I wanted to include an icon.png in the dashboardHeader using HTML, but couldn't get it to work. I ended up just doing it in CSS, which is fine.

So my general question: is there a way to include HTML code in the all sections of the dashboardPage by referencing an external HTML file, similar to what is done by creating the custom.css or should all the HTML changes just be done in the CSS file as well? I want to better understand how to take a hybrid approach with HTML (putting HTML in external file) and use best practices with Shiny. The external file options to include CSS, HTML and JS get a bit confusing, such as using: include vs using tags$head(tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css", href = "custom.css")). Hoping for more of a big picture explanation.

messages.author: 51708af3af54863b
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Dashboard and HTML
parts: To follow-up on this, the easiest way for me to conceptualize this is the ur.R script is simply just the index.html file (or defining it), which I guess should be obvious. What I've struggled with in viewing it this way is that the script doesn't always come out the way you would expect in putting together the index.html or at least it's not always obvious how to do so. For example in the shinydashboard package, it doesn't seem that you can place HTML in the dashboardHeader function, which has made less than optimal for putting new elements in the header (or at least I haven't figured out a good way to do this).

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Dashboard and HTML
parts:
Thanks Joe, I did notice that and we'll keep that in mind. 

I think ultimately just using the index.html is the best solution. What I struggle with is some things seem trivial through the ui.R and some trivial through the html.index, but blending the two is the challenge. For example, putting something like below straight in the index file is straightforward:

Hello Sir, <span class="hint--bottom" data-hint="Thank you!">hover over me.</span>

But, if we want to have the ui.R file generate the above script it's not straightfoward. Also, if we want to make changes later in the ui.R file then there needs to be a system in place to add the new ui.R generated html script to our final index file. I guess it's hard to know when you've hit a wall with the ui.R file and trying to implement something like the script above is not efficient. Just wondering if others had "best practices" ideas/experience in using both the ui.R script in combination with a final html.index.

This is pretty close:

tagList(
"Hello Sir,",
tags$span(class="hint--bottom", "data-hint"="Thank you!",
"hover over me."
)
)

Although admittedly this will differ in that there will be an extra space to the left and right of "hover over me" I believe--that's a bug we need to fix.
